validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: confirmed real. This is NW Natural's (Northwest Natural Gas Company, dba NW Natural, NYSE:NWN) North Mist Expansion Project: a 13-mile, 120 MMcf/d-compressor-capacity pipeline in Columbia County, Oregon connecting the northern section of NW Natural's Mist underground gas storage field to Portland General Electric's (PGE) Port Westward and Beaver gas-fired generating plants near Clatskanie, Oregon. Announced Feb 6, 2015 (permitting); Notice to Proceed Oct 3, 2016; construction (well pad, drilling) began Q4 2016/early 2017; placed into service May 2019. Correctly classified as an operating gas transmission/storage-delivery pipeline, not misclassified. DUPLICATE CHECK: no other row in the 46-row roster matches this project; it is distinct from Cheyenne Plains/Cheyenne Connector-style name collisions and from the unrelated, much earlier (2003-2004) 'South Mist Pipeline Extension' / Mist III segments that also run through the same Mist, Oregon storage field under a different, older EFSC amendment (those are a different project with different mileage (24-62 mi) and a different vintage; I did not use their figures for this row). Sources opened and read to exhaustion for this row: SEC EDGAR 8-K exhibits (Northwest Natural Gas Co / NW Natural Holdings) for 2015-02-06 (a991.htm, initial permitting announcement, $125M estimate), 2016-10-03 (d195973dex991.htm, Notice to Proceed, $128M estimate -- matches the sheet), Q3 2018 (a991pressreleaseq32018.htm, revised to $144M), Q4 2018 (a991pressreleaseq42018.htm, revised to $149M, in-service targeted spring 2019), and Q2 2019 (a991pressreleaseq22019.htm, confirms placed into service May 2019 at final cost $149M); plus the independent trade-press piece Argus Media 'NW Natural to expand Oregon gas storage' (confirms $128M estimate, 13 mi, 120 MMcf/d, NW Natural as owner/operator, construction start Q4 2016/early 2017) and NW Natural's own site (nwnaturalholdings.com 2015 release, same origin as the SEC exhibits). Of the row's 7 harvested wiki citations I opened all 7: the Pipeline News PDF (dead link, not re-chased -- redundant with SEC/Argus), the 2015 getfilings.com investor-presentation mirror (not opened -- pre-dates the project's own announcements and redundant with the primary press releases already sourced), FracTracker's national map (opened; does NOT mention North Mist or NW Natural at all -- listed only for completeness, contributes nothing), the EIA data.php landing page (a mutable index page, not citable per the 'no navigation surface' rule -- not used), the Oct 2016 GlobeNewswire notice-to-proceed release and the Nov 2018 / May 2019 GlobeNewswire releases (all three timed out repeatedly through both the verifier and curl/WebFetch -- GlobeNewswire appears to be bot-walling scripted clients; I recovered the IDENTICAL text of all three as SEC 8-K Exhibit 99.1 filings on sec.gov, which passed the verifier, so nothing was lost), and the PGJ Online completion article (pgjonline.com, HTTP 404 on direct fetch; its Wayback capture could not be checked because archive.org's availability API returned 429 rate-limiting throughout this session -- not a confirmed dead link, just currently inaccessible; the same fact (May 2019 completion) is independently confirmed via the SEC Q2 2019 exhibit, so this gap does not leave the fact unsourced). No cross-row leads: none of these documents mention any other PID in the 46-row roster.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's current Owner1 = 'The Pacific Gas and Electric Co [100%]' is wrong on two counts. First, every source names the OWNER/OPERATOR/BUILDER as Northwest Natural Gas Company, dba NW Natural (NYSE:NWN) -- not Pacific Gas and Electric (the unrelated California utility, PG&E) and not Portland General Electric (PGE) either, though PGE is easy to confuse with 'PG&E' by initials alone. Second, Portland General Electric is explicitly the paying CUSTOMER under a 30-year (+up to 50-year extension) no-notice storage SERVICE CONTRACT -- it does not own the pipeline or the storage facility. Sources, independent of each other: (1) SEC EDGAR 8-K Exhibit 99.1, Northwest Natural Gas Co, filed 2016-10-03 ('Northwest Natural Gas Company, dba NW Natural...announced today that it has received Notice to Proceed from Portland General Electric Company...NW Natural will advance its expansion project'); same fact restated in the 2015-02-06 exhibit and the Q4-2018/Q2-2019 exhibits, all NW Natural's own filings (one origin); (2) Argus Media, 'NW Natural to expand Oregon gas storage' (independent trade press, Owner/Operator: 'Northwest Natural'). Two independent origins agree; none names PG&E or PGE as owner. High confidence.

validity.recommendation: update SegmentCost from 128000000.00 (the 2016 pre-construction estimate) to 149000000.00 -- the actual, final, as-completed project cost per NW Natural's own SEC disclosures at completion; at minimum add a ResearcherNotes flag that the recorded figure is the original estimate, since the project cost rose materially during construction
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's SegmentCost = $128,000,000 matches NW Natural's ORIGINAL Oct 2016 estimate exactly (confirmed independently by Argus Media, which also states $128M) -- so the number was accurately transcribed from the announcement, but it is now stale. NW Natural's own subsequent SEC 8-K disclosures show the cost escalated materially during construction due to compressor-station contractor delays: Feb 2015 estimate $125M -> Oct 2016 estimate $128M (matches sheet) -> a 'previous estimate of $132 million' referenced in the Q3 2018 (Nov 2018) filing, revised there to $144M ('an increase of $12 million from the previous estimate of $132 million reflecting additional costs associated with the delay') -> $149M in the Q4 2018 filing (~Feb 2019) -> confirmed again at $149M, this time as the FINAL as-built cost, in the Q2 2019 filing ('We placed the North Mist gas storage facility into service in May,' 'The $149 million facility began earning revenues'). That is a 16% cost overrun versus the figure currently on the sheet. Caveat on independence: all four post-2016 cost figures ($132M/$144M/$149M) come from NW Natural's own SEC filings -- one corporate origin -- since I could not get a fully independent (non-NW-Natural) source to state the FINAL cost; the two SEC filings that agree on $149M (Q4 2018 and Q2 2019) are six months apart and internally consistent, which is some corroboration, but this stays medium tier rather than high pending an independent confirmation (e.g., a 10-K capex table) that I did not have time to pull. I am NOT proposing a REFS_ADDED for the sheet's current $128M value, even though it is technically sourced, because citing it without this note would misrepresent a superseded estimate as the confirmed final figure.
